_note: Scarborough's reading rope, as the organising frame for the Science of Reading hub. The eight strands and their two halves come from Hollis Scarborough's model; the mapping of which Upshift material serves which strand is ours, and so is every word of the descriptions. The counts are not written here -- the page reads them from the content so a strand cannot claim material it does not have.
source: The eight strands and the two halves are Hollis Scarborough's reading rope (2001).
intro: Eight strands, two halves. Word recognition becomes automatic; language comprehension becomes strategic. Fluency is where the two weave together, which is why it is not a ninth strand.

strands.name: Background knowledge
strands.what: What a reader already knows about the thing the text is about. A text about a glacier is harder if you have never heard of one.

have.label: Knowledge Threads
have.blurb: Every article regrouped by what it is about, each topic running K through 6, with the five minutes to run before you read.

strands.name: Vocabulary
strands.what: Knowing what the words mean, and enough about each one to use it rather than only recognise it.

have.label: Teach a Word
have.blurb: Say it, use it, write it, in about ten minutes a word.

strands.name: Language structure
strands.what: Syntax and grammar: how a sentence is put together, and what the parts of it are doing.

have.label: Sentence Lab
have.blurb: Combine, expand, and because/but/so — on sentences from an article they have read, with the answer key taken from the article's own harder version.

strands.name: Verbal reasoning
strands.what: Inference and evidence: working out what a text implies but does not say, and proving it from the words on the page.

have.label: Mysteries
have.blurb: A case a week, every grade. Every one is a claim-and-evidence task in disguise: a short story, four suspects, and the proof sitting in the text.

strands.name: Literacy knowledge
strands.what: How texts work: print concepts, text features, and the shapes a nonfiction text comes in.

have.label: Text feature articles
have.blurb: Articles that take the feature itself as the subject — the glossary, the heading, the caption, the arrow.

strands.name: Phonological awareness
strands.what: Hearing and moving the sounds in words, before any letter is involved.

have.label: Basic Reading workbooks
have.blurb: The scope and sequence in teaching order, each skill with its workbook and key.

strands.name: Decoding
strands.what: Turning letters into sounds reliably enough that the word arrives without effort.

have.label: OG concept packs
have.blurb: One concept across the whole family of skills it covers.

have.label: Lesson builder
have.blurb: Pick a skill and it writes the lesson, the word lists and the workbook.

strands.name: Sight recognition
strands.what: Words read instantly, without sounding out — which is where every decoded word ends up with enough practice.

have.label: Sight word lists
have.blurb: Eleven lists, in the order the workbooks teach them.

bridge.name: Fluency
bridge.what: Where the two halves weave together. A reader who decodes accurately but slowly is spending on the words what they need for the meaning.
bridge.blurb: A one-minute read on any passage, with words correct per minute, accuracy and how it sounded.
